Fixed by the 2.4.0 parser: long-form columns take the raw cell; title_fallbacks reclassified as a data-loss warning.

title: 2.3.0 migration: acceptance criteria were set Approved on import before slices existed, so the immutability trigger permanently blocked slice binding and v_phase_exit read zero forever. Fixed by the 2.4.0 parser (ACs land Proposed) plus this pass's carry-over: all mappable ACs bound to their slice while Proposed, then approved - order is load-bearing, approve-then-bind is impossible.

Production-bound compose sets MSSQL_PID: Developer, which Microsoft licenses for development/test only — a licence violation once ACMP serves the real committee. Fix: MSSQL_PID=Express (free production licence) in both environments (slice P21). Express limits are all satisfied here: recordings live in S3 (10 GB/DB cap fine), jobs are Hangfire not SQL Agent, and the custom mssql-server-fts image installs Full-Text Search independent of edition (gated by U3 spike).

Object-store bucket names were hardcoded consts, so every environment wrote to the same buckets — breaking per-environment isolation (AC-083). FOUR sites, not the three first recorded: UploadRecording.cs, GetRecordingUrl.cs, DeleteRecording.cs (all 'acmp-recordings') AND Topics AttachFileToTopic.cs ('acmp-topics'), which the original write-up missed. The fourth is the more serious one in cloud: deploy/aws/02-s3.sh provisions ONE bucket per environment for recordings + attachments, no bucket named 'acmp-topics' exists there, and the app's IAM policy grants no s3:CreateBucket to invent it — so topic attachment would have failed outright on AWS. Fixed in slice P22: StorageOptions (Storage:RecordingsBucket / Storage:AttachmentsBucket) injected into all four handlers; defaults reproduce the on-prem MinIO split so no existing object moves, and the cloud compose points both at ${ACMP_S3_BUCKET}.

title: sqlserver-init.sh guarded the mandatory Keycloak RCSI setting with DATABASEPROPERTYEX('keycloak','IsReadCommittedSnapshotOn'), which is NOT a valid DATABASEPROPERTYEX property name and returns NULL. Since `NULL = 0` is never true, the guarded ALTER never fired and READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT was left OFF on the Keycloak database — the exact deadlock-prone configuration ADR-0036 exists to prevent. Caught by the U2 spike (RCSI read back NULL despite a healthy Keycloak). Fixed by reading the flag from sys.databases.is_read_committed_snapshot_on in both the guard and the verification echo; the U2 re-run then reported 'the fixed guard fired' and RCSI=1. The idempotency-under-live-connection pass before the fix was a false positive (the ALTER simply never ran).

The backup bind mount is unwritable by the process that writes backups. SQL Server writes the .bak itself, from inside its container, as uid 10001 (mssql) — not as the cron user running backup.sh. Docker creates a missing bind source ROOT-OWNED 0755, so every BACKUP DATABASE fails with 'Cannot open backup device ... Operating system error 5(Access is denied.)'. The failure mode is what makes it severe: it appears only in a 02:00 cron log, names an OS error rather than a permission model, and until someone reads that log the deployment looks backed up while never having written a single .bak. Latent in the P18b on-prem script too (it worked only because the directory happened to be created by hand). Caught by the P23 U4 restore drill BEFORE any cloud backup existed. Fixed in slice P23: backup.sh probes the mount from inside the container before it starts and refuses with the exact remediation (sudo install -d -o 10001 -g 10001 -m 0755 <dir>), and deploy/runbooks/cloud-backup-dr.md carries it as a one-time prerequisite.

SQL Server EXPRESS forces AUTO_CLOSE ON for user databases, and an auto-closing database TEARS DOWN the full-text population — global search silently indexes nothing. This is an edition-change defect that arrives with PH-5: the on-prem Developer edition did not do it, Express does, and it is NOT inherited from `model` (verified live on the spike instance: model auto_close=0 while Acmp, keycloak and a scratch database were all 1). With AUTO_CLOSE ON the database shuts down whenever the last connection drops. The consequence is not merely a cold first query: it aborts the asynchronous full-text crawl. The U3 spike reproduced it end to end — an indexed Arabic row sat at populate-status 1 with 0 items indexed for over two minutes and CONTAINS returned 0 rows, because each poll connected, restarted the database, and killed the crawl it was measuring; the measurement was destroying what it measured. Setting AUTO_CLOSE OFF took the identical row through 1:0 → 1:1 → 4:1 → 0:1 and CONTAINS = 1 within about 15 seconds. Severity is driven by the failure MODE: nothing errors. Search returns zero results, the API logs are clean, the index exists, IsFullTextInstalled reports 1 and the word-breaker is present — every check we had said healthy while AC-060/AC-061 global search would have returned nothing in the cloud. It also masqueraded as flakiness for a full day (U3 'failed all 4 runs after passing earlier', recorded undiagnosed) because whether the crawl beat the next disconnect depended on machine load. Fixed in deploy/scripts/sqlserver-init.sh: both the app database and the Keycloak database are set AUTO_CLOSE OFF behind an is_auto_close_on guard so re-runs are a clean no-op (unlike RCSI this option needs no exclusive access, so no ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE). The U3 gate sets it on its scratch database too, so the spike now exercises the configuration we actually ship. Verified: full spike re-run 17 passed / 0 failed, crawl completing in ~6 seconds.
